If [MATH: y = 2\arsinh{x^2},] then find [MATH: \dfrac { extrm{d}y}{ extrm{d}x}.]
EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
[MATH: ewcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{ m arsinh} olimits} ewcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{ m arcosh} olimits} ewcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{ m artanh} olimits} ewcommand{\sech}{\mathop{ m sech} olimits} ewcommand{\csch}{\mathop{ m csch} olimits} ewcommand{\coth}{\mathop{ m coth} olimits} ewcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{ m arsech} olimits} ewcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{ m arcsch} olimits} ewcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{ m arcoth} olimits}]

The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic sine function is [MATH: \dfrac{ extrm{d}}{ extrm{d}x}(\arsinh x) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x^2+1}}.]

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

[MATH: (dy)/(dx)|= (d)/(dx)(2arsinh x^{2}); = 2 ⋅ (d)/(dx)(arsinh x^{2}); = 2 ⋅ (1)/(sqrt((x^{2})^{2} + 1)) ⋅ (x^{2})^{′}; = 2 ⋅ (1)/(sqrt(x^{4} + 1)) ⋅ 2x; = (4x)/(sqrt(x^{4} + 1)).]

The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic cosine function is [MATH: \dfrac{ extrm{d}}{ extrm{d}x}(\arcosh x) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x^2-1}}.]

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

[MATH: (dy)/(dx)|= (d)/(dx)(arcosh (x + 1)); = (1)/(sqrt((x + 1)^{2} − 1)) ⋅ (x + 1)^{′}; = (1)/(sqrt((x^{2} + 2x + 1) − 1)) ⋅ 1; = (1)/(sqrt(x^{2} + 2x)); = (1)/(sqrt(x(x + 2))).]

EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
[MATH: ewcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{ m arsinh} olimits} ewcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{ m arcosh} olimits} ewcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{ m artanh} olimits} ewcommand{\sech}{\mathop{ m sech} olimits} ewcommand{\csch}{\mathop{ m csch} olimits} ewcommand{\coth}{\mathop{ m coth} olimits} ewcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{ m arsech} olimits} ewcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{ m arcsch} olimits} ewcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{ m arcoth} olimits}]

Here, we have the product of two functions [MATH: u(x) = e^{2x}] and [MATH: v(x)=\artanh{x}.] So, we apply the product rule:

[MATH: w^{′}(x)|= (e^{2x})^{′} ⋅ artanh x + e^{2x} ⋅ (artanh x)^{′}; = 2e^{2x} ⋅ artanh x + e^{2x} ⋅ (1)/(1 − x^{2}); = 2e^{2x}artanh x + (e^{2x})/(1 − x^{2})_(⏟)_(y(x))]

Therefore, [MATH: y(x) = \dfrac{e^{2x}}{1 - x^2}.]
